selected.title: Australia's second largest veggie company admits 'cartel conduct'
selected.summary: Perfection Fresh Australia has admitted fixing the price of broccoli, cauliflower and lettuce sold to Aldi stores in New South Wales.
selected.why: Major producer admits illegal price-fixing cartel conduct in supermarket supply chain.
selected.fullText: Perfection Fresh admits fixing the price of vegetables sold to Aldi in NSW - ABC News Skip to main content Skip to news navigation, settings and search Explore the ABC news iview listen Loading ABC News News Home Perfection Fresh admits fixing the price of vegetables sold to Aldi in NSW Share Share article Perfection Fresh admits fixing the price of vegetables sold to Aldi in NSW By Justine Longmore ABC Rural Topic: Consumer Protection Posted Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 1:52pm Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 1:52pm Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 1:52pm , updated Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 4:37pm Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 4:37pm Mon 26 Oct 2026 at 4:37pm ALDI vegetable supplier Perfection Fresh has admitted to price fixing. ( ABC Rural: David Claughton ) In short: Perfection Fresh Australia has admitted engaging in "cartel conduct" on 11 occasions, 2019–2020. The company admitted fixing the price of vegetables sold to Aldi in NSW. What's next? The ACCC says the company has agreed to pay a $12m fine, subject to court approval. abc.net.au/news/perfection-fresh-admits-to-aldi-vegetable-price-fixing/107308678 Link copied Share Share article Australia's second-largest fresh produce supplier, Perfection Fresh Australia, has admitted to "cartel conduct" by fixing the price of broccoli, cauliflower and iceberg lettuce sold to Aldi stores in New South Wales. The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) began civil action in the Federal Court in September 2025 against four vegetable-growing companies, and three individuals, including Perfection Fresh. The group was accused of working together to illegally fix the price of fresh produce sold at Aldi stores in NSW, Victoria and Queensland between 2018 and 2024. The ACCC accused four vegetable suppliers of fixing the price of fresh produce. ( ABC News: Anna Chisholm ) The ACCC said Perfection Fresh had admitted to engaging in cartel conduct on 11 occasions between 2019 and 2020. Perfection Fresh has agreed to pay a $12 million penalty, subject to Federal Court approval at a later date. The case against the remaining suppliers — Hydro Produce, Veli Velisha Fresh Produce and Velisha National Farms, and M Fragapane & Sons — is continuing. Luke Woodward says cartel behaviour can increase prices and harm consumers. ( Supplied: ACCC ) In a statement, ACCC Commissioner Luke Woodward said cartel conduct "undermines competition". angle: A $12m fine may be insufficient penalty to deter cartel behaviour if it costs less than the profit from price-fixing.
